Elena —

Great questions. Per our discussion, we've sketched a pragmatic approach that balances operational predictability with customer protection. Key points below; I've attached a simple spreadsheet that models remedies under different uptime profiles (Redwood-Remedy-Model-v1.xlsx).

Summary proposal (draft language + economics):

1) Schedulable exceptions ("planned maintenance windows")
- Customers and Redwood can agree to up to X recurring weekly windows (e.g., Sun 02:00-04:00 PT). Events within those windows are excluded from monthly uptime calculations if Redwood provided >=72 hours notice and the window was published in the Console.
- For non-recurring planned events longer than 4 hours, Redwood will notify 5 business days in advance; exclusion applies once acknowledgement is recorded.

2) Uptime & latency SLOs (examples for contract):
- Hosted tier: 99.70% monthly availability (standard).
- Dedicated tier: 99.95% monthly availability.
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 300ms for <512 token requests (region-dependent).

3) Monetary remedy model (monthly cap + tiers)
- Remediation is monthly and pro-rated by outage minutes outside schedulable exceptions.
- Tiered credit bands: 0.10–0.50% below SLO = 5% monthly invoice; 0.51–2.00% = 10%; >2.00% = 20%.
- Monthly cap = 25% of that month's Redwood invoice for the impacted services (we can set a lower cap for pilots).

4) Exception guardrails
- Maintenance that causes partial region impact will be prorated to affected region usage; cross-region failover behavior is considered in calculation.
- For known maintenance scheduled during high-traffic agreed windows, Redwood will offer additional throttle controls and pre-warming where possible.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to draft contract language for the SOW exclusion and remedy bands.
- Marissa to run the remedy model against Acme's projected monthly token volume (workbook attached).
- Elena/Acme to confirm acceptable cap (25% or lower) and any preferred recurring windows.

I'll follow up with the draft SOW language by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,

Nikhil Sharma

Elena —

Looping in a short draft of contract language (below) to use as starting point for procurement/legal redlines. This is intentionally concise so your legal team can drop it into the SOW. Happy to expand if you prefer more granular definitions.

Draft SOW clause (for discussion):
"Planned Maintenance and Schedulable Exceptions: Customer and Redwood may mutually agree to recurring maintenance windows ("Schedulable Exceptions") during which scheduled activities shall be excluded from the calculation of monthly Availability for purposes of calculating remedies. Redwood will provide notice at least seventy-two (72) hours prior to any recurring maintenance window and five (5) business days prior to any non-recurring scheduled maintenance longer than four (4) hours. Schedulable Exceptions shall be published in the Redwood Console and recorded in the Parties' change log."

Remedy banding (proposal):
- Availability >= SLO: no credit
- Availability < SLO and >= SLO - 0.50%: 5% credit of monthly charges for impacted services
- Availability < SLO and >= SLO - 2.00%: 10% credit
- Availability < SLO - 2.00%: 20% credit
- Monthly cap: 25% of monthly charges unless otherwise agreed in writing

Open items from legal/procurement perspective:
- Define the default recurring window (we suggest Sun 02:00-04:00 PT) and allow customers to propose alternatives.
- Want to confirm whether credits are the sole remedy; Acme legal may request a definitive statement.
- Clarify interactions with security patching (are emergency security patches excluded?). Our standard practice is that emergency security patches are excluded from remedies if notice was reasonable and the patch addresses a CVSS >=7 vulnerability.

Marissa — once you run the model against Acme's volumes, please add two variants: 1) pilot cap = 10% 2) standard cap = 25%.

Elena — can you confirm whether your procurement team prefers credits or a combination (credits + one-time service rebates) for the pilot? If credits only, we'll bake that into the template.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
